attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as his assertion.

semantics.note: The normalisation keeps both parts: the warehoused value and the six-month installation rate for one quarter's sales. It is a firm present-tense assertion.

contract.note: The plain reading (about US$200bn or more, an aggregate deployment rate, the latest NVIDIA quarter) is ordinary and not stretched either way. The result is unresolved under any reasonable period or valuation choice, because no inventory census exists in the packet.

evidence.note: CBRE measures absorption in North American data-center markets. It does not measure GPU inventory or installation throughput.
Reports Amazon receiving hardware it could not yet power, from August 2026 on. That is a later period and a single company, so it cannot establish the global balance for the target quarter.

reviews.rationale: Supporting the claim needs a comprehensive valuation of sold but uninstalled NVIDIA GPUs, plus matched shipment and commissioning data. The packet has neither. CBRE capacity data and a later Amazon-only report are context only. Nothing in the packet contradicts the claim either.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense assertion. Dropping 'blatantly, alarmingly obvious' removes only rhetoric. 'Cannot afford' is evaluative but can be read as a factual claim.

contract.note: Reading 'cannot afford' as a financial inability to fund dependable service is ordinary. It could also mean the service is uneconomic, and the contract flags this. The choice of reading and period matters, but neither reading is settled by the packet.

evidence.note: Confirms an outage on April 15, 2026 within the period. It gives no cause linked to inability to pay, and outages alone are insufficient under the contract.
A company disclosure of the $30bn Series G (Feb 2026). It weighs against financial inability but does not show that dependable service was affordable.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents an outage and a large funding round, but has no cost assessment for dependable service and no link between outages and a funding shortfall. Neither the support condition nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion. The CNBC mention that follows is separate.

semantics.note: Faithful, a firm present-tense claim. 'Even if said numbers were real' is a concession, not an antecedent.

contract.note: The per-company reading and the Q1 2026 window are evaluator choices. Under the H1 2026 or FY2025 periods, Anthropic's filing would decide its part. A pooled reading would remain open. So the choices matter even though the contract says they do not.

evidence.note: The Anthropic S-1 (filed Oct 26, 2026) puts subscription revenue at 20% in H1 2026 and 17% in FY2025. That weighs strongly against Anthropic's part, but the period is not the contract's Q1 2026.
OpenAI's subscriber count and enterprise share do not establish its revenue share from subscriptions or delivery cost.

reviews.rationale: Anthropic's S-1 shows subscriptions at only 20% of H1 2026 revenue, which makes a Q1 subscription majority highly unlikely. It is still a different period, so it counts only as context. The packet has no Q1 revenue mix or subsidy data for OpenAI or Cursor, and no matched Q1 figure for Anthropic.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the antecedent and both alternatives. It is a firm counterfactual conditional ('would have to'). Reading 'inference costs' as spending fits the context.

contract.note: Requiring an enforceable reliability mandate before scoring keeps to the speaker's 'forced' antecedent.

evidence.note: Anthropic voluntarily raised its limits after adding compute (May 2026). Nothing forced it to provide stable service, so the antecedent is not shown.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, Anthropic being forced to provide a stable service, is not shown to have happened by the evaluation date. Under policy, a conditional whose antecedent has not occurred or is unknown is not scored.
